prompt: Hand-roll base64 encoding: index the 64-character alphabet yourself, regroup bytes into 6-bit chunks, and pad the final partial group with '=' signs. java.util.Base64 is not allowed.
explanation: Base64 regroups 8-bit bytes into 6-bit chunks, so three bytes (24 bits) become exactly four alphabet characters. Shifting the three bytes into one 24-bit int and then pulling out (block >> 18) & 63, (block >> 12) & 63 and so on is the cleanest way to cross the byte boundaries. The padding rule falls straight out of how many real bytes the last group had: a missing byte contributes zero bits and one '=' character, which is how a decoder later knows to throw those bits away.
hints: charFor is an if / else-if ladder over four ranges; within a range the answer is (char) ('A' + index) style arithmetic.
Combine the group with (b0 << 16) | (b1 << 8) | b2, treating missing bytes as 0, and remember how many were real.
Emit the first two characters always; emit the third only when the group had at least two bytes and the fourth only when it had three, using '=' otherwise.
